audit_findings.title: Non-operating investment gain may be capitalized and double-counted with cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $29 million pre-tax, 4.5% of the $642 million anchor; at most approximately $0.91 per share across the supplied scenarios before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in FY2025 OE, the one-time gain raises the anchor and is capitalized through every forecast period while the resulting cash is also included in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, the Company recognized a pre-tax realized net gain of $ 29 million in connection the sale of an investment, which has been presented within the Other income (expense) line of the accompanying consolidated statement of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the gain but not its inclusion in OE. Even assuming the full pre-tax amount was erroneously retained, the mechanical effect is small relative to the $15.57-$21.24 valuation range and the $7.54 gap between market price and bull value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $642 million FY2025 OE calculation to the cash-flow statement and other income, then rerun after removing the $29 million if it was retained.

audit_findings.title: Post-quarter 10K Projects consideration is either dilution or a cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 2.75 million shares, or 0.52% of the 530.588 million denominator; approximately $79.1 million at the supplied $28.78 price, equivalent to about $0.15 per current share
audit_findings.mechanism: Stock settlement increases fully diluted shares; cash settlement reduces excess cash or creates a bridge claim.
audit_findings.evidence: There is a fixed component, that represents an amount of $ 70 million due that will be satisfied either by the issuance of 2,333,333 shares of Class A Common Stock, the number of which was determined by dividing $ 70 million by $ 30 per share, or in cash for an amount determined by multiplying 2,333,333 shares by the share price on the trading day immediately preceding issuance at the sole discretion of WMG, and a contingent component that represents an amount of approximately $ 13 million that is contingent upon certain purchase price adjustments as specified in the Agreement, and will be satisfied at the sole discretion of WMG either by the issuance of up to 416,667 shares of Class A Common Stock or in cash for an amount determined by multiplying 416,667 shares by the share price on the trading day immediately preceding issuance.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, but the settlement form and whether the fully diluted denominator already includes it are unresolved. At the contractual maximum, dilution reduces bull value by only about $0.11 per share, while an equivalent cash payment reduces value by about $0.15 per share, neither large enough to alter the valuation range materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the August 2026 settlement notice and post-settlement cap table; rerun either with the actual issued shares or with the actual cash payment deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven earnings may omit the acquisition reinvestment required to sustain them
audit_findings.magnitude: $241 million of FY2025 business and music-rights acquisitions, equal to 37.5% of the $642 million anchor; mechanical sensitivity of approximately $5.40-$7.53 per share if all were recurring reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-generated earnings enter the OE anchor or forecast growth, while acquisition spending may be omitted when only reported capital expenditures are deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used in investing activities of $340 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 consisted of $46 million relating to investments and acquisitions of businesses, $195 million to acquire music-related assets, and $139 million relating to capital expenditures, partially offset by $40 million of proceeds from the sale of investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The $241 million outlay is demonstrated; whether it represents recurring maintenance, discretionary growth, or spending already deducted from OE is unresolved. Its scale is large enough to change intrinsic value materially if a substantial portion is required to sustain the earnings and growth being valued.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to the $46 million business-acquisition and $195 million music-rights purchases, separate organic from acquired earnings, estimate maintenance acquisition spending from filed history, and rerun the anchor and growth cases accordingly.

audit_findings.title: Bain's preferred return is a senior economic claim on Beethoven JV cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $135 million of Bain contributions at June 30, 2026; the filed 8% preference implies a $10.8 million annual hurdle before adjustments; future effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Bain's preferred return and 50% ownership reduce Beethoven cash attributable to WMG common equity and restrict how much JV cash can be included in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the joint venture, we are also required to pay Bain a preferred return on the equity it invests in WMBC prior to the Company earning a return on its investment in the joint venture.
audit_findings.explanation: The senior claim is demonstrated, but the FY2025 OE anchor largely predates Beethoven's acquisition activity and does not expressly credit its future earnings. The issue becomes valuation-relevant as JV acquisitions contribute to forecast growth or consolidated cash, so it should be monitored rather than treated as a demonstrated current anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Maintain a separate Beethoven schedule showing contributed capital, the 8% preference, quarterly distributions, WMG-attributable OE and restricted JV cash; rerun when Beethoven earnings or cash are included in the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Tempo consolidation can mismatch consolidated cash flows with WMG's 50.1% claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $439 million of acquired catalog assets, 49.9% non-WMG ownership and an approximately $73 million option; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation, working-capital movements, capital spending and cash can be added to OE or the bridge at 100% even though WMG owns 50.1%; crediting the remaining earnings also requires recognizing the option cost.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 5, 2025, WMG Tempo Holdco LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Acquisition Corp. and an indirect subsidiary of the Company, which has majority representation on the board of WMG Tempo Holdco LLC, acquired a 50.1 % interest in Tempo Music, a proprietary music rights acquisition platform, for consideration of $ 77 million, including transaction costs, with an option, exercisable on or prior to November 30, 2027, to acquire the remaining 49.9 % of Tempo Music for approximately $ 73 million, subject to contractual adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: Tempo's consolidation and minority ownership are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not trace Tempo's components through the $642 million OE anchor or the $618 million cash bridge. The mismatch may affect value, but its net size cannot be established from the available figures.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a Tempo-only reconciliation of attributable income, depreciation and amortization, working capital, capital spending, interest, cash and debt; allocate only WMG's economic share and deduct the approximately $73 million option before crediting the remaining 49.9%.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may not capture scheduled restructuring cash payments
audit_findings.magnitude: At June 30, 2026, $102 million had been paid during FY2026 across the two plans and $45 million remained accrued; approximately $115 million of the 2025 Plan's stated $200 million total cash expenditure remained after cumulative payments, plus the $7 million 2024 Plan accrual, or about $0.23 per share combined
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid restructuring cash is a one-time claim against bridge cash; capitalizing an anchor that reverses the accrual without recognizing settlement cash would also overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company anticipates that the Plan will result in cash expenditures of approximately $200 million of which $170 million is expected to be paid by the end of fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest cash balance already reflects payments made through June 2026. Even treating approximately $122 million as an additional unpaid bridge claim produces only about a $0.23-per-share reduction, roughly 1.5% of bear value, so it does not materially change the valuation conclusion. This does not establish whether the FY2025 OE calculation handled accrual reversals correctly.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2025 and FY2026 restructuring charges, working-capital adjustments and payments, then deduct any unpaid amount once in the bridge rather than capitalizing it as a recurring OE expense.
